sdpdd.title: TESS Science Data Products Description Document, EXP-TESS-ARC-ICD-0014 Rev F (Twicken et al. 2020, NASA/TM-20205008729)
quotes: Subtracting TIMECORR from TIME will give the light arrival time at the spacecraft rather than at the solar system barycenter.
TPS and DV operate on light curves generated by Presearch Data Conditioning (PDC).
RAW_CNTS ... ADU ... Raw, uncalibrated target image. FLUX ... e-/s ... Calibrated, cosmic ray removed, background subtracted target image.

instrument_handbook.title: TESS Instrument Handbook v0.1 (Vanderspek, Doty, Fausnaugh et al., draft of 6 December 2018)
quotes: During the image stacking process, pixel values are examined in groups of N : the highest and lowest values are discarded, and the sum is used in creating the stack. [...] the cost is a reduction in the effective exposure time by (N-2)/N [...] Pre-launch simulations calculated that the optimal value for N was 10.

During a momentum dump, the angular momentum is removed from the reaction wheels by firing the thrusters while the ACS keeps the spacecraft pointing stable. [...] During those five minutes, and for ~5-10 minutes thereafter, the spacecraft stability will be reduced.

At perigee, the spacecraft reorientation required for data downlink changes the camera temperatures by 1-2 deg C: camera temperatures return to nominal within 1.5-2 days after return to science orientation.
Each camera is equipped with a lens hood to minimize the levels of stray light from the Earth or Moon striking the detectors.
Pixel Size 15 um square; Lens Custom 146 mm, f/1.4; Bandpass 600-1040 nm; Camera FOV 24 x 24 deg (Table 2.1, Instrument Characteristics).

pl_name.label: Planet Name
pl_name.description: Planet name most commonly used in the literature

discoverymethod.label: Discovery Method
discoverymethod.description: Method by which the planet was first identified

disc_facility.label: Discovery Facility
disc_facility.description: Name of facility of planet discovery observations

tran_flag.label: Detected by Transits
tran_flag.description: Flag indicating if the planet transits its host star (1=yes, 0=no)

pl_controv_flag.label: Controversial Flag
pl_controv_flag.description: Flag indicating whether the confirmation status of a planet has been questioned in the published literature (1=yes, 0=no)

pl_orbper.label: Orbital Period [days]
pl_orbper.description: Time the planet takes to make a complete orbit around the host star or system

pl_rade.label: Planet Radius [Earth Radius]
pl_rade.description: Length of a line segment from the center of the planet to its surface, measured in units of radius of the Earth

pl_radelim.label: listed in the 'Limit Column' of the definitions table, next to pl_rade
pl_radelim.description: the page gives no definition of the values

pl_bmasse.label: Planet Mass or Mass*sin(i) [Earth Mass]
pl_bmasse.description: Best planet mass estimate available, in order of preference: Mass, M*sin(i)/sin(i), or M*sin(i), depending on availability, and measured in Earth masses

pl_bmasselim.label: listed in the 'Limit Column' of the definitions table, next to pl_bmasse
pl_bmasselim.description: the page gives no definition of the values

pl_bmassprov.label: Planet Mass or Mass*sin(i) Provenance
pl_bmassprov.description: Provenance of the measurement of the best mass. Options are: Mass, M*sin(i)/sin(i), and M*sini

pl_ratror.label: Ratio of Planet to Stellar Radius
pl_ratror.description: The planet radius divided by the stellar radius

pl_ratdor.label: Ratio of Semi-Major Axis to Stellar Radius
pl_ratdor.description: The distance between the planet and the star at mid-transit divided by the stellar radius. For the case of zero orbital eccentricity, the distance at mid-transit is the semi-major axis of the planetary orbit.

pl_orbincl.label: Inclination [deg]
pl_orbincl.description: Angle of the plane of the orbit relative to the plane perpendicular to the line-of-sight from Earth to the object

pl_trandep.label: Transit Depth [%]
pl_trandep.description: The size of the relative flux decrement caused by the orbiting body transiting in front of the star

pl_tranmid.label: Time of Conjunction (Transit Midpoint) [days]
pl_tranmid.description: The time given by the average of the time the planet begins to cross the stellar limb and the time the planet finishes crossing the stellar limb.

st_teff.label: Stellar Effective Temperature [K]
st_teff.description: Temperature of the star as modeled by a black body emitting the same total amount of electromagnetic radiation

st_rad.label: Stellar Radius [Solar Radius]
st_rad.description: Length of a line segment from the center of the star to its surface, measured in units of radius of the Sun

sy_dist.label: Distance [pc]
sy_dist.description: Distance to the planetary system in units of parsecs

toi.label: TESS Object of Interest
toi.description: A number used to identify and track a TESS Object of Interest (TOI). TOIs are identified and numbered by the TESS Project. A TOI name has an integer and a decimal part of the format TOI-NNNNN.DD. The integer part designates the target star; the two-digit decimal part identifies a unique transiting object associated with that star.

tfopwg_disp.label: TFOPWG Disposition
tfopwg_disp.description: TESS Follow-up Observing Program Working Group (TFOPWG) Dispostion: APC =ambiguous planetary candidate CP =confirmed planet FA =false alarm FP =false positive KP =known planet PC =planetary candidate

pl_orbper.label: Planet Orbital Period [days]
pl_orbper.description: Time the planet takes to make a complete orbit around the host star or system.

pl_trandurh.label: Planet Transit Duration [hours]
pl_trandurh.description: The length of time from the moment the planet begins to cross the stellar limb to the moment the planet finishes crossing the stellar limb.

pl_trandep.label: Planet Transit Depth [ppm]
pl_trandep.description: The size of the relative flux decrement caused by the orbiting body transiting in front of the star.

pl_rade.label: Planet Radius [R_Earth]
pl_rade.description: Length of a line segment from the center of the planet to its surface, measured in units of radius of the Earth.

st_tmag.label: TESS Magnitude
st_tmag.description: Brightness of the host star as measured using the TESS-band in units of magnitudes as reported in the TESS Input Catalog.

st_rad.label: Stellar Radius [R_Sun]
st_rad.description: Length of a line segment from the center of the star to its surface, measured in units of radius of the Sun as reported in the TESS Input Catalog.

toi_created.label: TOI Creation Date
toi_created.description: Date on which the TESS Project identified the Object of Interest.

quotes.composite_table: By contrast, the goal of the PSCompPars table is to provide users with a table that is as complete as possible with a single row of data per planet. This indicates the PSCompPars table will necessarily include parameters from a variety of references for a given planet, indicating the set of reported parameter values may not be internally or physically self-consistent.
quotes.radius_from_mass: For planets that do have an empirically determined value for the planet mass $M_{p}$ but do not have an empirically determined value for the planet radius $R_{p}$, regardless of whether the planet has an empirically determined planet density $\rho_{p}$, we invoke the mass-radius relation of Chen & Kipping (2017) to derive the planet radius
quotes.calculated_reference: We do not report uncertainties for any parameter value that has been calculated. The associated reference column for a parameter value that has been calculated reads "Calculated Value,"
quotes.planet_criteria: The mass (or minimum mass) is equal to or less than 30 Jupiter masses.
